newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Prime Minister John Major abruptedly ended his Asian tour today in order to dash back for tonight's crucial Commons vote. The Finance bill vote is the first significant test of Major's ability to carry through to his preferred election date on May 1st.
GAS FEELS PRESSURE AS COMPETITION HOTS UP

Nationwide gas competition for domestic customers is set to flourish under existing plans which state that domestic competition must be introduced fully by the end of 1998, following pilots schemes in the south west of England in 1996 and in the south east beginning next month. British Gas' soon-to-be-demerged supply arm is set to be squeezed.

Natwest Ventures, the development capital arm of the High Street bank grew strongly last year as a result of a boom in management buyouts. Natwest invested 285 million stg in transactions with a total value of 1.2 billion stg.
PACKER PUTS 160 MLN STG ON A HOT NUMBER IN SYDNEY HARBOUR
Kerry Packer, Australia's richest man is also a high class gambler. He has decided to invest 342 million Australian dollars (160 million stg) on a share in the Sydney Harbour Casino.
